metadata.notes: Scientific caveats retained; no graphics rights or publication approvals.

reviews.title_after: Windstorm Kyrill sweeps across Europe in a rapidly deepening cyclone
reviews.core_fact: On January 18, 2007, an intense European windstorm known as Kyrill crossed northwestern and central Europe, with damaging winds across several countries.
reviews.source_dependence: University Hamburg observing history and a European windstorm research archive describe the same cyclone from different meteorological/insurance perspectives.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Kyrill's maximum gusts were station-specific and its cyclone evolution included secondary cyclogenesis; do not claim one wind speed or impact hour for every country. A research archive's loss figures are model-based, not confirmed direct damage counts.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original track and pressure tendency with station-specific peak gusts and UTC-to-local date markers

reviews.title_before: Dust Storm — SOUTHWEST DESERT/LOWER GILA RIVER VALLEY, New Mexico
reviews.title_after: Blinding Lordsburg Playa dust contributes to an I-10 pileup
reviews.location_after: Lordsburg Playa along Interstate 10, southwest New Mexico
reviews.core_fact: On February 27, 2025, blowing dust reduced visibility along Interstate 10 west of Lordsburg, New Mexico, during an 11-vehicle fatal crash.
reviews.source_dependence: NOAA NCEI Storm Events and a local public-media investigation quoting New Mexico crash authorities corroborate date and general location, but crash-specific casualty attribution comes from law enforcement.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Police descriptions of weather as a contributing factor do not establish weather as the sole cause of each collision. New Mexico State Police reports three fatalities, while Storm Events entry metadata and narrative may use different fatality-attribution rules; do not infer meteorological fatality totals from vehicle count.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Lordsburg Playa road geometry with wind direction, time-logged visibility and incident marker, no graphic crash imagery

reviews.title_after: Repeated tropical downpours swell Kauaʻi streams and flood Hanalei
reviews.location_after: Hanalei River and north shore of Kauaʻi, Hawaii
reviews.core_fact: Heavy rain on March 13, 2006 contributed to flooding near the Hanalei River and bridge on Kauaʻi during a prolonged wet-weather episode.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Honolulu retrospective and NCEI Hanalei Storm Events record share a weather agency source lineage; the date is corroborated, individual impacts require separate chronology.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The Ka Loko Dam failure occurred early March 14, not March 13. Multiple rounds of March 2006 flooding had distinct meteorological causes and different community impact windows; do not conflate Hanalei bridge flooding with the next-day dam-break deaths.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original March 13–18 Hanalei rain totals and river chronology with separate March 14 dam-failure note

reviews.title_after: Tambora erupts days before the blast that alters the world's climate
reviews.secondary_publisher: University of Rhode Island volcanology research repository
reviews.core_fact: Scientific reconstructions describe a first major Plinian eruption at Tambora on April 5, 1815, preceding the much larger April 10–11 climactic eruption and subsequent global climatic effects.
reviews.source_dependence: Published 2014 volcanological reconstruction and original URI-hosted tephra research both rely in part on earlier stratigraphic analysis, not fully independent calendar-date testimony.
reviews.unverified_cautions: April 5 is the precursor eruption, NOT the April 10–11 climax responsible for most SO2/aerosol climate forcing. First eruption column-height estimates are model-based; 1816 'Year Without a Summer' is a subsequent climatic response, not April 5 local weather.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original two-stage Apr 5 versus Apr 10–11 eruption timeline plus separately timed global aerosol/climate response

reviews.title_after: The 1913 Death Valley temperature record remains official—and disputed
reviews.location_after: Greenland Ranch (Furnace Creek), Death Valley, California
reviews.secondary_publisher: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
reviews.core_fact: The official WMO archive still lists a 56.7°C (134°F) temperature observation recorded July 10, 1913 at Greenland Ranch in Death Valley, while subsequent peer-reviewed analysis challenges the validity of that original measurement.
reviews.source_dependence: The WMO official archive and peer-reviewed instrument-quality reanalysis disagree about validity; agreement is only that the 1913 entry exists and is dated July 10.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Official record-holder status does NOT prove the underlying 1913 thermometer observation is reliable. A 2026 peer-reviewed assessment identifies major warm-bias concerns, but published recommendations to revoke the record are not the same as official WMO revocation. Never present 56.7°C as an undisputed verified physical temperature.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original record-versus-reconstruction chart showing WMO-listed value, independent surrounding stations and explicit uncertainty bands

reviews.title_after: The Winooski River crests as Montpelier's downtown floods
reviews.core_fact: After heavy rainfall July 9–10, 2023, the Winooski River at Montpelier crested during the morning of July 11, inundating Vermont's capital.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Burlington hydrometeorological case analysis and USGS post-flood streamgage/high-water-mark report use separate agency hydrologic methods, though some source gauges are shared.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Rainfall had largely occurred the preceding day(s), while July 11 is the Montpelier river-crest and impact anniversary. NWS narrative cites 21.35 feet while city records cite about 21.29 feet: confirm precise gauge, datum and final quality control before quoting crest heights.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original July 9–11 rainfall and Winooski at Montpelier hydrograph overlay with rain onset vs crest distinction

reviews.title_after: Vostok Station measures Earth's official lowest surface air temperature
reviews.core_fact: The recorded surface-air temperature at Vostok Station, Antarctica, reached −89.2°C on July 21, 1983, the WMO-listed global observed minimum.
reviews.source_dependence: WMO record archive and British Antarctic Survey reconstruction refer to the same original Soviet station observation; BAS adds distinct meteorological mechanism analysis.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The −89.2°C is an official station thermometer observation at 02:45 UTC, not a satellite-inferred land-surface skin temperature or typical regional minimum. Do not equate satellite-derived colder snow-surface temperatures with this air-temperature record.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original station-elevation and inversion schematic with UTC marker and observed-air vs satellite-surface-temperature legend

reviews.title_after: The 1859 geomagnetic storm lights low-latitude skies and disrupts telegraphs
reviews.core_fact: A major geomagnetic storm and unusually widespread low-latitude aurora developed on September 2, 1859, after Carrington observed a solar white-light flare on September 1.
reviews.source_dependence: NASA historical eyewitness analysis and Canadian government compilation of telegraph disruption accounts cite some shared 19th-century witnesses but independently document the September 2 impact day.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not date Carrington's solar flare to September 2; that was observed September 1. The geomagnetic storm's aurora and telegraph disturbances crossed local midnight and historic local-time zones. This is SPACE WEATHER, not a tropospheric thunderstorm. Estimates of a modern Dst equivalent are model-dependent.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Sun–Earth timeline: Sep 1 flare, Sep 2 auroral/telegraph response, geographic observations

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Joaquin batters the Bahamas while its track remains uncertain
reviews.location_after: Samana Cays, Crooked Island and southeastern Bahamas
reviews.core_fact: On October 1, 2015, Hurricane Joaquin's eye moved across or near the Samana Cays area as destructive hurricane conditions affected the central and southeastern Bahamas.
reviews.source_dependence: Contemporaneous U.S. NHC advisory and Canadian national hurricane-season retrospective share NHC best-track inputs but independently document broad event/date; CDEMA supplies regional impacts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: October 1 versus October 2 matters: NHC advisory reports Joaquin over Samana Cays October 1, with other distinct island crossings during October 2. Do not attribute Joaquin's exact storm-center track to South Carolina's simultaneous floods; those resulted from a separate low with transported moisture. NHC advisory classification changed later.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Oct 1–2 slow-loop center positions with Bahamas islands and separately dated warnings

reviews.title_after: Apollo 12 launches into electrified cloud and triggers lightning
reviews.core_fact: On November 14, 1969, Apollo 12 launched from Kennedy Space Center through clouds with high electric fields, and lightning struck the vehicle early in ascent.
reviews.source_dependence: NASA mission-history engineering record and NWS spaceflight weather chronology share underlying launch investigation but provide institutional context for electrification and forecasts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NASA details strikes around 36 and 52 seconds; don't present this as two independent natural pre-existing thunderstorms. Subsequent scientific work describes vehicle/plume-triggered lightning in electrified cloud without active conventional lightning. Archive photos have their own rights/credit requirements.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original launch trajectory and cloud charge/triggered-lightning mechanism timeline without republishing Apollo film

reviews.title_after: Toronto wakes to a damaging ice storm and widespread power outages
reviews.secondary_publisher: Public Safety Canada Canadian Disaster Database
reviews.core_fact: Freezing rain on December 21–22, 2013 coated Toronto and southern Ontario in ice, causing widespread damage and significant power disruptions on December 22.
reviews.source_dependence: City of Toronto municipal recovery records and Public Safety Canada's national disaster registry have separate custodians; both cite ECCC's meteorological history and Toronto Hydro outage records.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The storm began December 21 and outages continued for days. Ice accretion varied by gauge and neighborhood; outage customer counts differ between initial December 22 and later restoration estimates. '30 mm' refers an upper regional ice estimate, not citywide uniform glaze.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original December 21–22 freezing-rain/temperature cross-section and phased outage timeline

reviews.title_after: Windstorm Martin tears across southern France after Lothar
reviews.core_fact: On December 27, 1999, windstorm Martin struck southwestern and southern France, following the separate Lothar storm of December 26.
reviews.source_dependence: Météo-France chronology and French state reinsurance event archive date separate Martin and Lothar systems but use overlapping wind/impact datasets.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Martin on December 27 and Lothar on December 26 were two distinct depressions; do not sum their national impacts or attribute northern France gusts from Lothar to Martin. Storm Martin continued into December 28 and nearby December 28 OTDwx UK Tay Bridge case is a different 1879 wind event, so consider hazard pacing.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original two separate cyclone tracks Dec 26 Lothar vs Dec 27 Martin with geographic wind-maximum divisions
